He said: "I said: 'Indeed Allah is odd and loves the odd: the heavens are seven, the earths are seven, He provides from seven, brings forth from seven, and I see it only in the seven remaining of Ramadan.'" ʿUmar said: "My opinion agreed with your opinion." Then he struck my shoulder and said: "You are not the least learned of the people."

Zayd ibn Thābit and Bilāl said: It is the twenty-fourth night. Their evidence is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Ḥarb related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muʿāwiyah related to us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿah related to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḍābiḥī, from Bilāl, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth." [205] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 8/537, no. 24048.]]

It was said: It is the twenty-fifth night, indicated by what:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥāfiẓ informed us, together with others, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb related to us, saying: Baḥr ibn Naṣr related to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Wahb informed you, the report of one of them, Mālik ibn Anas, from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek it on the ninth, the seventh and the fifth." [206] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 8/536, no. 24038.]]

Others said: It is the twenty-seventh night, and this is the view of ʿAlī, Ubayy, ʿĀʾishah and Muʿāwiyah, indicated by what:

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūs informed us, saying: Abū Aḥmad Ḥamzah ibn al-ʿAbbās informed us in Baghdad, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Walīd al-Faḥḥām related to us, saying: Musawwad ibn ʿĀmir Shādhān related to us, saying: Shuʿbah informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār informed me, saying: I heard Ibn ʿUmar relate from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the Night of Decree that he said: "Whoever seeks it, let him seek it on the night of the twenty-seventh." [207] [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 4/311.]]

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us by reading to him, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAffān related to us, saying: ʿAmr al-ʿAnqarī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said:

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 97, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

We came to Ibn Mas'ud and asked him about Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree). He said: "Whoever stands in prayer for the whole year will attain it." It was said to him: "May Allah have mercy on Abu 'Abd al-Rahman! He knows that it is in the month of Ramadan and that it is on the twenty-ninth night." He said to us: "Abu al-Mundhir, I know that. But [I rely on] the sign that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us about, so we memorized it and counted." He said: "By Allah, it is indeed within what you make an exception of." We said: "Abu al-Mundhir, what is the sign?" He said: "The sun rises at that time like a basin, with no rays."

It is also narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) with my own ears, or else may my ears be deaf, saying: 'Laylat al-Qadr is the night of the twenty-seventh.'" [208] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/130.]]

Some of the Companions said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood in prayer with us on the night of the twenty-third for a third of the night. When it was the night of the twenty-fifth, he stood with us for half the night. When it was the night of the twenty-seventh, he stood with us the whole night."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "Allah, glorified and exalted, divided the words of this Surah among the nights of Ramadan. When He reached the twenty-seventh, He pointed to it and said: 'Hiya' (it)."

Some others said: "It is the night of the twenty-ninth."

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Laylat al-Qadr is the night of the twenty-seventh or the twenty-ninth, and the angels on that night are as numerous as the pebbles." [209] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/137.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, saying:
'Uyayna ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: My father told me, saying: Laylat al-Qadr was mentioned in the presence of Abu Bakra, and he said: "I will not seek it except in the last ten nights, because of something I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Seek it in the last ten nights, on the ninth remaining, or the seventh remaining, or the fifth remaining, or the third remaining, or the last night.'" [210] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/39.]] Abu Bakra, whenever the month of Ramadan entered, would pray throughout the rest of the year, and when the last ten nights entered, he would exert himself [in worship].

In sum, Allah concealed the knowledge of this night from the Ummah so that they would strive in worship during the nights of Ramadan, hoping to attain it, just as He concealed the Middle Prayer among the prayers, His Greatest Name among the names, the hour of response among the hours of Friday, His anger in disobedience, His pleasure in acts of obedience, and the Hour [of the Resurrection] among the times. This is out of mercy and wisdom from Him. And Allah knows best.

Chapter Three: On its signs and indications.

Abu 'Umar al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Sarakhsi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Yusuf told us, saying: al-Nadr narrated to us from Ash'ath, from al-Husayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning Laylat al-Qadr: "Among its signs is that it is a bright, clear night, neither hot nor cold; the sun rises the next morning without rays." [211] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/137, and something similar in Kanz al-'Ummal: 8/538, no. 24052.]]

Hamid ibn 'Umar said: "I was on the sea on the night of the twenty-seventh, and I took some of its water and found it sweet (without salt)."

Chapter Four: On its virtues and distinctive features.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Juhani narrated to us there, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Hasan informed us in Baghdad, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven." [212] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/309.]]

And in a hadith: "Indeed, the Devil does not come out on this night until its dawn breaks, and no one can be harmed on it by possession, disease, or any kind of corruption, and no sorcery of a sorcerer takes effect on it." [213] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/137.]]

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When Laylat al-Qadr comes, the angels who dwell at Sidrat al-Muntaha descend, and among them Jibril. Jibril descends with banners, placing one banner on my grave, one on Bayt al-Maqdis, one in al-Masjid al-Haram, and one on Mount Sinai. He does not leave any believing man or woman without greeting them, except one who is addicted to wine, one who eats pork, and one who is heavily perfumed with saffron." [214] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/137. al-Tadammukh means to smear oneself with perfume and to use it excessively.]]

Chapter Five: On its etiquette and what is recommended during it.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Mukarram told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Kahmas informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraida, that 'A'isha said to the Prophet (ﷺ):
"If Laylat al-Qadr comes to me, what should I say?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, You are Most Forgiving and You love forgiveness, so forgive me.'" [215] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/171.]]

Shurayh ibn Hani' narrated from 'A'isha, who said: "If I knew which night is Laylat al-Qadr, I would ask Allah for nothing in it except well-being."

Abu 'Umar al-Furati also informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Sahl informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn 'Isa told us, saying: Faris ibn 'Umar told us, saying: Salih told us, saying: al-'Umari narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'a, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers on Laylat al-Qadr [in congregation] has taken his share of Laylat al-Qadr." [216] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/138.]]

﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾ [[Surah al-Qadr: 3.]]

Abu 'Umar al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Musa informed us, saying:
Musa ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Abu Mus'ab told us, from Malik, that he heard from someone he trusted that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown the lifespans of people, and that the lifespans of his Ummah were short, so that they could not reach in deeds what others reach through a long life. So Allah gave him: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾

The scholars differed about the wisdom behind this specific number.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Kindi told us, saying:
'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatim told us, saying: It was recited to [Yunus] ibn 'Abd al-A'la: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
Maslama told us, from 'Ali ibn Lahi'a, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once mentioned four men from the Children of Israel who worshipped Allah for eighty years without disobeying Him for the blink of an eye. He named them: Ayyub, Zakariya, Hizqil the son of the old woman, and Yusha' ibn Nun. The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) marveled at this. Then Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, your Ummah marvels at the worship of these men for eighty years without disobeying Allah for the blink of an eye." He said: "Allah has sent down to you something better than that," and then he recited to him: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, [and said:] "This is better than what you and your Ummah marvel at." The Prophet (ﷺ) and the people with him were delighted by this. [217] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/567.]]

Abu 'Amr al-Furati also informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn 'Isa told us, saying:
Faris ibn 'Amr told us, saying: Salih told us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid ibn Abi Najih told us that the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who wore weapons in the cause of Allah for a thousand months. The Muslims marveled at this, so Allah, glorified be He, sent down: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾, meaning what that man wore of weapons in the cause of Allah.

It is said that this man was Samson (peace be upon him). His story, as reported by Wahb ibn Munabbih, is that he was a Muslim man whose mother had dedicated him as a nazirite. He was from a village in the lands of the Byzantines who worshipped idols, and his dwelling was a few miles from them. He would fight them alone, striving against them for the sake of Allah, gaining from them what he needed, killing, taking captives, and seizing wealth. Whenever he met them, he would meet them with a camel's jawbone, and no other weapon. When they fought him, he fought them, and when he grew weary and thirsty, pure water would gush for him from the stone that was in the jawbone, and he would drink until he was satisfied.

He had been given great strength in striking, and no iron chain or any other binding could hold him. He continued like this, striving in the cause of Allah and gaining his needs from them, and they could not overcome him in anything. Then they said: "You will not reach him except through his wife." So they entered upon his wife and offered her a reward. She said: "Yes, I will bind him for you." They gave her a strong rope and said to her: "When he sleeps, tie his hand to his neck until we come and seize him." When he slept, she tied his hand to his neck with that rope. When he awoke, he pulled with his hand and it snapped from his neck.

He said to her: "Why did you do that?" She said: "I wanted to test your strength, for I have never seen anyone like you." She then sent word to them: "I have bound him with the rope, but it did not avail anything." They sent her an iron chain and said: "When he sleeps, put it around his neck." When he slept, she put it around his neck, and when he awoke he pulled it and it fell from his hand and neck. He said to her: "Why did you do this?" She said: "I wanted to test your strength. I have never seen anyone like you in the world, O Samson. Is there nothing on earth that can overcome you?" He said: "Only one thing." She said: "And what is it?" He said to her: "Here, I will tell you about it." She kept asking him about it. He had a great deal of hair, and he said to her: "Woe to you! My mother had dedicated me as a nazirite, so nothing will ever overcome me, and only my hair can restrain me." When he slept, she tied his hand to his neck with the hair of his head, and it bound him. She then sent word to the people.

They came and seized him. They cut off his nose, pierced his ears, and gouged out his eyes. They paraded him between the sides of the city, which was a city of pillars. The king of them had gone up to the top of it with the people, to watch what would be done to Samson. When they had mutilated him and placed him standing, Samson called upon his Lord to give him power over them. He was commanded to take hold of two of the pillars of the city upon which the king and the people with him were standing. He pulled both of them together, and Allah restored his sight and whatever they had taken from his body. The minaret fell upon the king and those upon it of the people, and they perished under its rubble. [[At length in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/465.]]

It was also said: In past times a man did not deserve to be called "worshipper" until he had worshipped Allah for a thousand months, which is eighty-three years and four months. So Allah, glorified be He, gave the Ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him) a night better than a thousand months, in which they could worship.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "The kingdom of Solomon lasted five hundred months, and the kingdom of Dhu al-Qarnayn lasted five hundred months. So the meaning of the verse may be: 'The Night of Decree is better for whoever attains it than what Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn (peace be upon them) possessed.'"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ashqar told us, saying: Zayd ibn Akhram told us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: 'Alqama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Yusuf ibn Mazin al-Rasibi, who said: A man stood up before al-Hasan ibn 'Ali and said: "You have blackened the faces of the believers! You went to this man, meaning Mu'awiya, and gave him your allegiance." He said: "Do not reproach me, may Allah have mercy on you, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown the Banu Umayya ascending his minbar one by one, and that grieved him. Then there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾ — [the thousand months] that the Banu Umayya will rule."

Al-Qasim said: "O Allah, the rule of the Banu Umayya is enough for us. It turned out to be exactly a thousand months, neither more nor less." [218] [[Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 3/170; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 9/197.]]

The exegetes said: "A righteous deed on the Night of Decree is better than the deed of a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree." Al-Rabi' narrated from Abu al-'Aliya: "The Night of Decree is better than a lifetime of a thousand months." Mujahid said: "The greeting of the angels and the Spirit upon you that night is better than the greeting of all creatures upon you for a thousand months. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾."

Talha ibn Musarrif recited "tanazzalu" (تنزل) lightly, from descent (al-nuzul).

﴿And the Spirit﴾ means Jibril, according to the view of most exegetes (tafsir). What supports this is what Qatada narrated from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "When Laylat al-Qadr comes, Jibril descends in a great company of angels, praying and greeting every servant standing or sitting who remembers Allah, glorified be He." [219] [[Zad al-Masir: 8/287.]]

Ka'b and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "The Spirit is a group of angels whom the [other] angels do not see except on that night. They descend from sunset until the break of dawn."

al-Waqidi said: "He is a great angel [among the greatest of angels in creation], who is created from among the angels." [[From Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/496.]]

﴿Therein﴾, i.e., on the Night of Decree, ﴿by the permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ that Allah, glorified be He, has decreed and determined for that year until the next, as in His saying in Surah al-Ra'd: ﴿They guard him by the command of Allah﴾ [[Surah al-Ra'd: 11.]], i.e., by the command of Allah.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra' told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite "min kulli imri' salam" (مِنْ كُلِّ امْرِئٍ سَلامٌ). This recitation is also narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and 'Ikrima. It has two possible meanings:

The first: that the "min" points to the angel, meaning "from every angel, peace."

The second: that "min" means "upon" (ʿalā), so that the meaning is: "Upon every man among the Muslims is peace from the angels," like His saying: ﴿And We helped him against the people﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 77.]], meaning "against the people." However, the correct recitation is that of the common people, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative transmitters upon it, and because it agrees with the script of the Mushafs (copies of the Qur'an), since there is no "ya'" in it.

His saying ﴿Salam hiya﴾ is the completion of the sentence at ﴿from every matter﴾. Then He began: ﴿Salam hiya﴾, i.e., the Night of Decree is peace and goodness in its entirety, with no evil in it.

al-Dahhak said: "Allah does not decree on that night except safety. As for the other nights, Allah decrees in them both trials and safety." Mujahid said: "It is safe; the Devil cannot do any evil in it or cause any harm."

al-Sha'bi and Mansur ibn Zadhan said: "It is the greeting of the angels on the Night of Decree to the people of the mosques, from sunset until the break of dawn. They pass by every believer and say: 'Peace be upon you, O believer.'"

﴿Until the rising of the dawn.﴾ "Hatta" (حتى) is a particle of limit, and its sense here is "until the rising of the dawn." Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "matla'" (مَطْلِعِ) with a kasra on the lam, while others read it with a fatha. The fatha is the preferred reading, because "maṭla'" with a fatha on the lam means "ṭulū'" (rising): one says "ṭalaʿat al-shams ṭulū'an wa maṭla'an" (the sun rose). As for "maṭli'" with a kasra on the lam, it denotes the place of rising, and the noun has no meaning in this context, since it is used here in the sense of the verbal noun. And Allah knows best.
